newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS-Wolford net profit up 9 pct in first half.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Wolford net profit up 9 pct in first half.

text.p: Austria's hosiery maker Wolford posted a nine percent jump in net earnings to 106.9 million schillings ($9.8 million) in the six months to October 31, pulled up by growth abroad, and forecast record full-year sales.

The company predicted sales would reach 1.7 billion schillings in 1996/7, up from last year's record 1.475 billion, and said it aimed to double the number of its stores around the globe to 200 by the end of the business year.

"We expect an increase of sales of 16 percent and net profit growth to be higher than sales growth in 1996 to 1997," chief financial director Karl Michael Millauer told Reuters in an interview late on Monday.
Sales rose eight percent to 829.3 million schillings in the first half, while pre-tax earnings increased to 158.7 million schillings from 146.6 million a year ago.
Millauer said the dividend level would be raised from its current 15 schillings providing full year results were in line with forecasts.

"We will certainly increase the dividend, as we expect a record result this year," he noted. "I see no reason why we can't justify a profit to earnings ratio of 30 to 35 schillings as we are still a growth company in sales and net profit."
The company had seen a shift in ordering patterns, resulting in a 20 percent growth in prompt order intake, Millauer explained.
"If that strength continues then we will have higher sales in the second than in the first half," he said.
Wolford had no plans to diversify, preferring to focus on improving technology, expanding its distribution and enlarging its capacity, Millauer said.
He forecast strong sales growth in 1997/8.

The luxury hosiery and lingery maker, which supplies fashion houses such as Yves St Laurent and Versace and has an export quota of 82 percent, had seen massive sales growth in the new markets of the United States (134 percent) and in Britain (51 percent).
Millauer said the immediate priority would be to build up Wolford's brand recognition in the United States, ahead of its debut on the New York stock market in 1997.

The company, which has just one production plant based in Bregenz near the border with Switzerland, had no plans to build a second plant until 1998 at the earliest, he said. Wolford is targetting the United States for its second plant but U.S. sales must first exceed $30 million. For this year the firm has projected sales of $14 million.
Once the company had got a firm foothold in the U.S., it would look to strengthen its market share in Asia, Millauer noted.

The financial chief predicted a modest pick-up in Germany where sales have shrunk three percent after 20 percent growth in the past five years, but said the company neeeded to improve its sales strategy there.

The first phase of the company's current expansion programme is due to be completed by the end of January 1997, which Millauer said would ease capacity constraints in dying. Such problems had led to delays in delivering some 70,000 fixed orders for the slinky swimbody line, introduced in September, he said. ($ = 10.87 Austrian Schillings)
